brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.requirement: Herb planter of three cells side by side
requirements.evidence: Three full-depth piece cells in a straight line at axial (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0) on level 0, joined by joint bolts; open faces capped.

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: Each of the three cells holds a hex-bin-full-drain (drained, full depth) tray; each is filled with soil and planted (basil, mint, thyme). check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell straight planter row with a drained full-depth bin in each cell, filled with soil and planted with basil, mint and thyme. Configurator checks are clear. Drainage is the bin's drained shape; I have not verified water flow or material durability.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
